subsystems.name: Quantum sensor suite
subsystems.role: measures gravity, acceleration and time with far more precision than classical instruments, letting a robot navigate and map without GPS.

subsystems.name: Quantum planner
subsystems.role: solves scheduling, path-planning and task-allocation problems that grow too large for classical solvers.
parts: classical optimiser for pre- and post-processing

subsystems.name: Classical autonomy stack
subsystems.role: everything the robot actually does in real time — perception, control, manipulation.

subsystems.name: Hardened quantum housing
subsystems.role: keeps delicate quantum hardware alive through launch vibration, vacuum, thermal swings and radiation.

subsystems.name: Communication link
subsystems.role: carries plans and telemetry under long light-time delays.

buildSteps.title: Pick problems with a real quantum advantage
buildSteps.detail: Target tasks where quantum algorithms provably beat classical ones — large scheduling, sensor fusion, gravity-field inversion — rather than bolting quantum hardware onto ordinary control loops, which classical chips do faster and more reliably.

buildSteps.title: Build the sensing core
buildSteps.detail: Laser-cool atoms in a small vacuum cell, split and recombine them, and read interference fringes that shift with acceleration or gravity.

buildSteps.title: Space-qualify the sensor
buildSteps.detail: Replace lab lasers and pumps with rugged, efficient versions, test through vibration, thermal vacuum and radiation, and shrink the optics so it fits a rover.

buildSteps.title: Develop hybrid algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Encode mission-planning problems for a quantum processor, with a classical computer preparing inputs and checking outputs. Validate on simulators and small hardware first.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with classical autonomy
buildSteps.detail: Let the quantum planner propose routes or schedules while a conventional controller keeps the robot safe, executing and rejecting bad plans in milliseconds — quantum modules are advisors, not pilots.

buildSteps.title: Fly a technology demonstration
buildSteps.detail: Put the sensor and planner on an analogue rover or a servicing robot and run realistic maintenance and prospecting tasks.

buildSteps.title: Operate through delay
buildSteps.detail: Run the quantum planner on the ground where hardware can be large and cooled, uplinking plans to a robot that must act autonomously between contacts.

buildSteps.title: Scale to teams
buildSteps.detail: Extend planning to many robots sharing one task, coordinating through the communication link.

prerequisites.why: cold-atom experiments have flown on the ISS and sounding rockets; none yet fly as operational navigation instruments.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum processors robust enough for field use
prerequisites.why: today's machines need careful laboratory conditions and are error-prone, so they cannot run unattended on a spacecraft.
useful quantum answers need errors suppressed well below current levels.
cosmic rays and solar particles disturb qubits and sensors in ways not yet fully characterised or designed around.
robots on the Moon or Mars act alone for minutes to hours, so plans and data must survive long gaps.

pathway.milestone: quantum sensors in orbit and in the lab; classical autonomous space robots doing inspection and simple servicing
pathway.unlocks: component technology and a baseline of classical autonomy.

pathway.milestone: quantum gravimeters and inertial sensors on rovers for GPS-free navigation and subsurface mapping
pathway.unlocks: precise positioning and resource prospecting where satellite navigation is unavailable.

pathway.milestone: ground-based quantum optimisation for multi-robot task scheduling and trajectory design
pathway.unlocks: faster planning for complex servicing, assembly and mining campaigns.

pathway.milestone: radiation-tolerant quantum co-processors flying on the robot itself
pathway.unlocks: on-the-spot planning in deep-space missions with long communication delays.

pathway.milestone: teams of robots extracting and processing resources with quantum-secured links
pathway.unlocks: self-sustaining operations far from Earth — if the hardware survives the environment.
